what: Albemarle is one of the world's largest lithium producers, mining and processing lithium for electric vehicle batteries, and it also makes bromine-based flame retardants and refinery catalysts.
customers: Battery makers and carmakers for lithium, electronics and construction firms for bromine, and refiners for catalysts.
money: lithium carbonate and hydroxide for batteries
bromine for flame retardants and other specialty chemicals
moat: Low-cost lithium resources in Chile and Australia and the processing plants to convert them, which take years and billions to replicate.
risks: Lithium prices collapsed, taking revenue from $9.6B to $5.1B in two years
A reported operating loss after write-downs on projects started at the top of the cycle
opportunities: 6.8 times free cash flow with $1.4B of free cash flow
Analysts see about 70% upside, with 21 covering the stock
The bromine and catalyst businesses are steady and unrelated to lithium, which supports the company through the trough
watch: Lithium prices and whether production volumes keep growing through the downturn.
